5 Pack of Cultures (Your Choice) + Twist-Off Tool
Abalone (Pleurotus cystidiosus)
species.description: Abalone Mushroom, (Maple Oyster Mushroom), is a choice edible with small cream-white caps, strongly decurrent gills and a short central or eccentrical stem are characteristic. In culture this mushroom presents black droplets (called 'coremia') that might be easily confused with black mold contaminants. Substrate: straw, hardwood sawdust (cottonwood, oak, maple, sweetgum elm, beech, poplar). Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/70-80F

species.name: Agarikon (Fomitopsis offcianalis)
species.description: Found in the old growth forests off the coast of America and in Europe and grows on conifers, particularly Douglas-fir and larch. Agarikon may be the oldest mushroom in the world. It is described as the "elixir of long life" by the Greek physician Dioscorides in Materia Medica. The mushroom is yellowish when young but soon becomes white with red and grey coloration as it ages.

species.name: Almond Mushroom (Agaricus blazei)
species.description: Almond Mushroom (Agaricus blazei) is a choice edible, with a somewhat sweet taste and fragrance of almonds. Also well known as a medicinal mushroom. This culture will die under refrigeration or if temperatures drop below 55F — should NOT be ordered during winter months but perfect for growing in the summer heat. Substrate: Crop straws, such as rice straw, wheat straw, corn straw, cottonseed shell along with compost and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 73-80F/62-91F

species.name: Almond Mushroom (Agaricus subrufescens)
species.description: This culture will die under refrigeration or if temperatures drop below 55F — should NOT be ordered during winter months but perfect for growing in the summer heat. Substrate: Crop straws, such as rice straw, wheat straw, corn straw, cottonseed shell along with compost and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 73-80F/62-91F

species.name: Amber Jelly Fungus (Exidia crenata)
species.description: This edible jelly fungus is especially common in the Midwest, where it appears on hardwood sticks and branches (Mostly Willow) after late spring rains and throughout the mushroom season. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust

species.name: Amber Nam (Pholiota nameko)
species.description: Nameko - Amber Nam (Pholiota nameko). Substrate: hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/50-65F

species.name: Antler Reishi (Ganoderma multipilium)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Artist's Conk (Ganoderma applanatum)
species.description: Artist's conk is exceptionally common in Maine, growing on older sugar maples and many other hardwood trees, usually persisting for years. Artists use these mushrooms for etched designs when fresh and for landscape painting when dried. They can be displayed on a table or shelf. They become almost as hard as a block of wood and will last for many years. Contains polysaccharides and triterpenoids with various medicinal implications. Can be made into a medicinal tea.

species.name: Aspen Oyster (Pleurotus populinus)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust (aspen). Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-74F

species.name: Bear's Head (Hericium americanum)
species.description: Bear's Head (Hericium americanum) is a species with long spines and a branched fruiting body, found only in North America, fruiting from dead wood or live trees. When young and fresh, generally considered choice edibles with a fine flavor and texture similar to fish or Lobster. Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Bear's Head (Hericium americanum) Wild Maine Strain
species.description: Wild Maine strain (Near Mud Pond), cloned from the mushroom in the picture. Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Beech Wild Strain (Hypsizygus tessulatus)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-65F

species.name: Beef Steak (Fistulina hepatica)
species.description: Beefsteak mushrooms (also known as ox tongue mushroom) are a relatively rare polypore. The mushroom itself is red, resembling meat, and gives off a red juice when sliced. Grows on the wood of oaks and other hardwoods.

species.name: Berkeley's Polypore (Bondarzewia berkeleyi)
species.description: Berkeley's polypore grows on oaks and other hardwood trees. The fan shaped caps grow in overlapping clumps from the bases of oak trees, each capable of growing to 10 in. diameter. Various shades of white to pale grey, cream, beige or yellow. Has little taste on its own — can be used to take on other flavours in dishes, much like tofu, and can be used as a meat substitute.

species.name: Big White Beech Wild Strain (Hypsizygus tessulatus)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-65F

species.name: Birch Polypore (Piptoporus betulinus)
species.description: The birch polypore is a common bracket fungus that grows almost exclusively on birch trees. It has long been known that the Birch Polypore has medicinal uses — used as a tonic for the immune system, as an antiseptic to clean wounds and promote healing, a plaster that is microporous, antifungal and antiseptic. Maine Wild Strain.

species.name: Bitter Oyster (Panellus stipticus)
species.description: Bitter Oyster (Panellus stipticus) is one of several dozen species of fungi that are bioluminescent. The luminescence is localized to the edges of the gills and the junction of the gills with the stem and cap. Considered not edible and sold as a novelty only. Substrate: Sawdust/Woodchips. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-80F/60-75F

species.name: Black Fungus (Annulohypoxylon sp.)
species.description: Annulohypoxylon archeri is commonly used in the cultivation of Snow Fungus (Tremella fuciformis) — one of the foremost medicinal and culinary fungi of China and Taiwan. Tremella fuciformis is a parasitic yeast that does not form an edible fruitbody without parasitizing another fungus. Annulohypoxylon archeri is its preferred host.

species.name: Black Hoof Mushroom (Phellinus linteus)
species.description: Black hoof mushroom is shaped like a hoof, has a bitter taste, and in the wild grows on mulberry trees. In Korean traditional medicine, the mushroom is consumed in the form of hot tea. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, mulberry trees. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Black Morel (Morchella importuna)
species.description: Morchella importuna is a black morel that appears to be limited to landscaping sites, gardens, planters, and so on. In North America it is fairly common in the northwest, where it appears in urban settings in late winter and early spring.

species.name: Black Morel (Morchella mel) 8
species.description: Morel species "mel-8" is a black morel with ridges that darken with maturity, pits and ridges that are primarily vertically oriented, and a cap attached to the stem with a small but noticeable groove. Virtually indistinguishable from many other black morels on the basis of physical features alone.

species.name: Black Pearl King Oyster (Pleurotus eryngii ostreatus)
species.description: The Black Pearl Oyster is an oyster mushroom hybrid from Japan, a cross between a European and an Asian Pleurotus ostreatus. Less finicky than Pleurotus eryngii, able to grow very well indoors. Fast substrate colonizer that fruits dense, meaty mushrooms. Colonization Temperature: 65-78F. Fruiting Temperature: 50-68F, Humidity: 90-95%, Air exchanges: 4-8 per hour.

species.name: Black Poplar (Agrocybe aegerita)
species.description: Black Poplar (Agrocybe aegerita) is an easy-to-grow edible mushroom with a mellow nutty flavor. Popular culinary mushroom in Italy, grown across Asia, Australia and the U.S. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/50-60F

species.name: Black Reishi (Ganoderma formosanum)
species.description: Black Reishi (Ganoderma formosanum) is a rare polypore mushroom used for its medicinal properties. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Black Reishi (Ganoderma neo japonicum)
species.description: Ganoderma neo-japonicum is a rare polypore mushroom used for its medicinal properties, said to be less bitter than other species of Reishi. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Black Reishi (Ganoderma sinense)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Blue Brat Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Blue Chanterelle (Polyozellus multiplex)
species.description: Blue Chanterelle (Polyozellus multiplex) are mycorrhizal with conifers — especially spruces and firs — in low, wet areas; usually growing in dense, fused clusters; northern and montane North America (from the Pacific Northwest to Maine, and in the Rocky Mountains); summer and fall.

species.name: Blue Oyster (Pleurotus columbinus)
species.description: A blue tinted oyster mushroom with cultivation requirements similar to the pearl or common oyster mushroom. Fruits easily on a wide range of substrates. As with all Oyster mushrooms, needs plenty of fresh air to develop normally. The blue coloration is much more pronounced in early stages of growth. Substrate: Straw, sawdust, wood chips, coffee grounds, newspaper and cardboard. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-80F

species.name: Blushing Bracket (Daedaleopsis confragosa)
species.description: Commonly known as the thin walled maze polypore or the blushing bracket. A plant pathogen that causes white rot of injured hardwoods, especially willows. The whitish underside turns gray-brown as the fruit body ages, but bruises pink or red. Found all year and is common in northern temperate woodlands of eastern North America, Europe, and Asia.

species.name: Blushing Morel (Morchella rufobrunnea)
species.description: Blushing Morel (Morchella rufobrunnea) grows in disturbed soil or in woodchips used in landscaping. Differs from other Morchella species by its urban or suburban habitat preferences, in the color and form of the fruit body, and the bruising reaction. A process to cultivate morels now known to be M. rufobrunnea was described and patented in the 1980s.

species.name: Bolles Bear's Head (Hericium americanum) Wild Strain
species.description: Bolles Bear's Head (Hericium americanum) was found on the Bolles trail in the White Mountains. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Branched Oyster (Pleurotus cornucopiae)
species.description: Also known as Popcorn Oyster. Oyster mushrooms look like oyster shells and have a mildly seafood-like taste. Great sauteed in butter with salt and pepper, also nicely complement any soup, sauce or stir fry. Substrate: Straw, sawdust, wood chips, newspaper and cardboard. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/65-85F

species.name: Brick Cap (Hypholoma sublateritium)
species.description: Brick Cap (Hypholoma sublateritium) is a widely distributed mushroom found growing on hardwood trunks in the fall. Receiving increasing attention from commercial growers because it is considered edible and suited for cultivation. A close relative of Stropharia rugosoannulata (the wine cap). Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-75F/50-60F

species.name: Brick Cap (Hypholoma sublateritium) Maine Wild Strain
species.description: Cloned from wild specimens. Brick Cap (Hypholoma sublateritium) is a widely distributed mushroom found growing on hardwood trunks in the fall. A close relative of Stropharia rugosoannulata (the wine cap). Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-75F/50-60F

species.name: Brown Beech Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus)
species.description: Beech Clam / Buna Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus) is an edible mushroom native to East Asia. Most often found on beech trees, hence the common name Beech Mushroom. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-65F

species.name: Bulbous Honey Mushroom (Armillaria gallica)
species.description: Widely distributed east of the Rocky Mountains, typically found on the ground or near the bases of hardwoods. Usually a late-fruiting species, appearing in the colder weather of late fall and early winter.

species.name: Burnt Morel (Morchella eximia)
species.description: Morchella eximia is a fire-associated species, growing abundantly in recently burned forests.

species.name: Cauliflower Mushroom (Sparassis crispa)
species.description: Cauliflower mushroom (Sparassis crispa) is a popular edible mushroom found in Northern Europe and the United States. It feeds on the root zones of mature conifer trees. Can fruit on sawdust. Similar growth parameters to Maitake. Generally a difficult mushroom to cultivate. Fruiting Temperature: 55-65F

species.name: Chaga (Inonotus obliquus)
species.description: Chaga (Inonotus obliquus) is parasitic mainly on birch. The conk is irregularly formed and has the appearance of burnt charcoal. It is not the fruiting body of the fungus, but a sclerotia or mass of mycelium, mostly black because of the presence of massive amounts of melanin. Considered a medicinal mushroom.

species.name: Champignon (Agaricus brunnescens)
species.description: Substrate: Compost. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-77F/60-66F

species.name: Chestnut Mushroom (Pholiota adiposa)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust / Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-75F/50-70F

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods (Laetiporus conifericola)
species.description: Laetiporus conifericola is a species of polypore fungus found in western North America ranging from California to Alaska, where it grows on conifer trees, particularly fir, spruce, and hemlock.

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods (Laetiporus gilbertsonii)
species.description: Collected in California along Hwy 1. Growing on a dead Blue Gum eucalyptus. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/75-95F

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods (Laetiporus sulphureus)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/75-95F

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods (Laetiporus sulphureus) Wild Maine Strain 1
species.description: Wild Maine strain, cloned from wild specimens.

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods (Laetiporus zonatus)
species.description: Laetiporus zonatus is a species of polypore fungus in the family Fomitopsidaceae. Found in southwestern China, where it grows on oak.

species.name: Chicken Of The Woods White Pored (Laetiporus cincinnatus) Me L23
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/75-95F

species.name: Conifer Coral (Hericium abietis)
species.description: Hericium abietis is a choice edible growing on conifer stumps or logs in North America, producing a cream white fruit body up to 4-30 inches tall and wide. Substrate: Conifer, Fir & Douglas Fir sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Conifer Tuft (Hypholoma capnoides)
species.description: Hypholoma capnoides is an edible mushroom which fruits in clusters on conifer stumps and logs. It is typically a fall or winter mushroom.

species.name: Coral Tooth (Hericium coralloides)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Coral Tooth (Hericium coralloides) Iowa Wild Clone
species.description: Iowa wild cloned Coral Tooth (Hericium coralloides). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Corn Smut (Ustilago maydis)
species.description: A plant disease (huitlacoche) that grows on ears of corn. Blue-grayish with a soft and velvety texture. Has a very pungent earthy, sweet yet savory and woody taste with flavors of mushroom and corn. A culinary delicacy in Mexican cuisine used in soups, enchiladas, and sauces. Harvested two or three weeks after the corn has become infected.

species.name: Crown Tipped Coral (Clavicorona pyxidata) Maine Wild Strain
species.description: Crown-tipped Coral (Artomyces pyxidatus) — isolated Maine Wild Strain. Will colonize in roughly 3-4 weeks. Can be side fruited but best top fruited. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, grows well on Master's Mix. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/70-75F

species.name: Dancing Hens (Grifola frondosa)
species.description: Maitake - Dancing Hens (Grifola frondosa). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/50-65F

species.name: Dead Man's Fingers (Xylaria polymorpha)
species.description: Xylaria polymorpha, commonly known as dead man's fingers, is a saprobic fungus. A common inhabitant of forest and woodland areas, usually growing from the bases of rotting or injured tree stumps and decaying wood.

species.name: Dead Man's Fingers (Xylaria polymorpha) Maine Wild Strain
species.description: Cloned from wild specimens. Grew on just hardwood sawdust (HWFP). Maine Wild Strain.

species.name: Enoki Golden (Flammulina velutipes)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/40-60F

species.name: Enoki White (Flammulina velutipes)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/40-60F

species.name: Enoki Wild Strain (Flammulina velutipes)
species.description: Grows at warmer temps. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/40-85F

species.name: Florida Oyster (Pleurotus florida)
species.description: This is a summer strain of Pearl Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus). Color varies with increasing light intensity and temperature, from white-beige to greyish blue. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-85F/70-85F

species.name: Fluted Bird's Nest (Cyathus striatus)
species.description: Cyathus striatus, commonly known as the fluted bird's nest, is a common saprobic bird's nest fungus with a widespread distribution throughout temperate regions of the world. This fungus resembles a miniature bird's nest with numerous tiny 'eggs'; the eggs (peridioles) actually contain spores. Distinguished from most other bird's nest fungi by its hairy exterior and grooved inner walls.

species.name: Freckled Chestnut (Pholiota adiposa)
species.description: Chestnut - Freckled Chestnut (Pholiota adiposa). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust / Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-75F/50-70F

species.name: Garlic Scented Mushroom (Mycetinis scorodonius)
species.description: The garlic mushroom is an edible fungus that smells and tastes like garlic, and can be used as a substitute for garlic in meals. Found growing underneath coniferous and hardwood trees around the world.

species.name: Ghost Fungus (Omphalotus nidiformis)
species.description: Omphalotus nidiformis, or ghost fungus, is a gilled mushroom most notable for its bioluminescent properties. Its bioluminescence (blue-green color) is only observable in low light conditions. Only the gills glow. Its fruit bodies are generally found growing in overlapping clusters on a wide variety of dead or dying trees. Deadly poisonous — could be mistaken for an edible Pleurotus. Substrate: Variety of woods. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-80F/60-75F

species.name: Golden Chanterelle (Cantharellus cibarius)
species.description: A European strain. Smaller in size to their North American cousins but considered superior by many. Firm, meaty, golden mushrooms with an earthy, peppery flavor offset by a sweet, fruity undertone often compared to apricots. Chanterelles cannot be grown indoors — they are mycorrhizal and must form a relationship with conifer trees. Use liquid culture to create grain spawn and bury it near conifer trees. Can take years or even decades for chanterelles to establish.

species.name: Golden Chestnut (Pholiota sp.) Maine Wild Strain
species.description: Golden Chestnut (Pholiota sp.) — Cloned from wild specimens found at Hirundo park. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust / Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 65-75F/50-70F

species.name: Golden Oyster (Pleurotus citrinopileatus)
species.description: The golden oyster grows slower and is not as productive as other oyster mushrooms such as the pearl oyster. These mushrooms also need plenty of fresh air to develop normally. Substrate: Straw, hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/70-85F

species.name: Golden Oyster Wild Strain (Pleurotus citrinopileatus)
species.description: Iowa wild cloned Golden Oyster (Pleurotus citrinopileatus)(Holstgold). Substrate: Straw, hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/70-85F

species.name: Golden Treasure Oyster (Pleurotus citrinopileatus)
species.description: Golden Oyster - Golden Treasure (Pleurotus citrinopileatus). Substrate: Straw, hardwood chips and sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/70-85F

species.name: Green Elfcup Fungus (Chlorociboria aeruginascens)
species.description: Chlorociboria aeruginascens is a saprobic species commonly known as the green elfcup. Although the actual fruit bodies are infrequently seen, the green staining of wood caused by the fungus is more prevalent. Contains a quinone pigment called xylindein responsible for the characteristic bluish-green stain of wood. The use of this wood (known as 'green oak') goes back to 15th century Italy, where it was used in intarsia panels.

species.name: Grey Dove Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Grey Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Hed Khon Khao White Shiitake (Lentinus squarrosulus)
species.description: These grow and taste very similar to Shiitake. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/50-75F

species.name: Hedgehog Mushroom (Hydnum repandum)
species.description: The Hedgehog Mushroom fruit bodies grow singly, scattered, or in groups on the ground or in leaf litter in both coniferous and deciduous forests. Can also grow in fairy rings. Fruiting occurs from summer to autumn. Considered a good edible mushroom with a sweet, nutty taste and a crunchy texture. Some consider it to be the culinary equivalent of the chanterelle.

species.name: Hemlock Reishi (Ganoderma tsugae)
species.description: Hemlock Reishi (Ganoderma tsugae) is a form of Reishi that fruits on conifers, typically hemlocks. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Indian Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius)
species.description: Phoenix (Cool) - Indian Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood & Pine sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 75-85F/50-75F

species.name: Italian Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius)
species.description: Phoenix (Warm) - Italian Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust, Pine sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/50-82F

species.name: Ivory Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus)
species.description: Beech - Ivory Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-65F

species.name: Jack O Lantern Mushroom (Omphalotus olearius)
species.description: Jack-o'lantern mushroom is a large orange mushroom often found in clumps on decaying stumps, buried roots or at the base of hardwood trees. Its gills often exhibit a weak green bioluminescence when fresh. Poisonous to humans when eaten, whether raw or cooked, and typically causes vomiting, cramps, and diarrhea.

species.name: King Of Pearl (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: King of Pearl (Pleurotus ostreatus) is a high yielding (Sporeless) strain tolerant to a range of growing conditions and can be easily grown year round. Will produce cream color to grey to dark brown mushrooms depending on growing conditions, mostly temperature. Substrate: Pasteurized straw, Hardwood Sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/50-87F

species.name: King Oyster (Pleurotus eryngii)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: King Trumpet Oyster (Pleurotus eryngii)
species.description: King Oyster - King Trumpet Oyster (Pleurotus eryngii). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: King Tuber Oyster (Pleurotus tuber regium)
species.description: King Tuber Oyster (Pleurotus tuber-regium) is a tropical mushroom gaining interest in the U.S. The mushroom produces an underground tuber as well as a mushroom (both are edible). The cap curves upward to form a cup-like shape when mature. Can be grown on organic wastes such as corn, sawdust, cardboard. Mycelial growth occurs between 60 and 104F with optimum growth at 95F.

species.name: Korean Oyster (Pleurotus spodoleucus)
species.description: Korean Oyster (Cham-Neutari) (Pleurotus spodoleucus)

species.name: Late Oyster (Panellus serotinus)
species.description: Late oyster grows on the wood of both hardwood and softwood trees. In Japan, where it is called Mukitake, it is considered 'one of the most delicious edible mushrooms'. Dark green to olive when fresh, fading to yellowish or greenish. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-75F/40-55F (can fruit at warmer temps but fruits may have a lighter color)

species.name: Lingzhi Reishi (Ganoderma lingzhi)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Lion's Beard (Hericium erinaceus)
species.description: Lions Mane - Lion's Beard (Hericium erinaceus). Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust, hardwood logs. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Lion's Mane (Hericium erinaceus)
species.description: The Lion's Mane is a toothed fungus that forms tooth-like spine structures instead of gills. Spontaneously fruits on agar and sawdust substrates but may be slow to colonize grain spawn. Has been used for hundreds of years in Traditional Chinese Medicine — recent studies show certain compounds produce antioxidant effects, may regulate blood lipid levels and may reduce blood glucose levels. Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust, hardwood logs. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Lion's Mane Heat Tolerant (Hericium erinaceus)
species.description: Cloned from a wild Lion's Mane found in mid summer. Grew well indoors during a heatwave well into the 90's. Has been fruited in temps up to 103F. Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust, hardwood logs. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-95F

species.name: Lion's Paw (Hericium erinaceus)
species.description: Lions Mane - Lion's Paw (Hericium erinaceus) — can tolerate higher temps. Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust, hardwood logs. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-90F

species.name: Lion's Pride (Hericium erinaceus)
species.description: Lions Mane - Lion's Pride (Hericium erinaceus). Substrate: Hardwood chips and sawdust, hardwood logs. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-75F

species.name: Macrocybe titans
species.description: Macrocybe titans is a species of mushroom native to Florida, Central and South America. Found growing alone or in clusters in grassy or sandy areas, or in ground disturbed by landscaping. Common in Florida; tropical and subtropical in distribution.

species.name: Maine Oyster 2019 (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Cloned from wild specimens, October 31st (Halloween), Greenbush Maine. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-75F/50-75F

species.name: Maine Wild Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)

species.name: Milky Mushroom (Calocybe indica)
species.description: Milky Mushroom (Calocybe indica) is a commonly cultivated tropical mushroom that easily grows on a variety of substrates. Produces well on pasteurized straw and treated sawdust blocks. Favors a peat moss casing layer to stimulate fruiting. Excellent shelf life compared to common oyster mushrooms. This culture will die under refrigeration or if temperatures drop below 55F — should NOT be ordered during winter months. Substrate: Straw or sterilized sawdust (case with peat moss). Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 80-85F/85-95F

species.name: Nameko (Pholiota nameko)
species.description: Substrate: hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/50-65F

species.name: Natural Morel (Morchella snyderi)
species.description: One of western North America's so-called 'natural' morels — which means it appears in non-burned forests, rather than landscaping sites or burn sites.

species.name: New Zealand's Bush Shiitake (Lentinula novae zelandiae)
species.description: Lentinula novae-zelandiae can be cultivated commercially under controlled conditions, much like its close relative Lentinula edodes (Shiitake). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust (avoid soy hull supplementation). Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-78F/42-78F. This culture sourced from Australia.

species.name: Nilla Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Pearl Oyster - Nilla Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus). Substrate: Pasteurized straw, Hardwood Sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Oregon Polypore (Ganoderma oregonense)
species.description: Oregon Polypore (Ganoderma oregonense) is a form of Reishi that fruits on conifers, typically hemlocks and firs, in the Pacific Northwest. Able to form very large mushrooms and very similar to Ganoderma lucidum. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Paddy Straw (Volvariella volvacea)
species.description: Paddy Straw (Volvariella volvacea) is a mushroom that fruits only above 80F. Widely cultivated in Asia on rice straw. This culture will die under refrigeration or if temperatures drop below 55F. Substrate: Composted straw (preferably rice), cotton waste, hardwood sawdusts. The pH optimum for fruiting falls between 7.5-8.0. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 75-85F/80-110F

species.name: Pathfinder Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: MCM (Mossy Creek Mushrooms) Original Wild cloned Oyster from Washington State, USA.

species.name: Pear Shaped Puffball (Lycoperdon pyriforme)
species.description: The pear-shaped puffball grows on decaying wood, present throughout much of the world. Considered a choice edible when still immature and the inner flesh is white. Can be used fresh, or cut into thin slices for drying, which can then be pulverized for use as a flavoring powder.

species.name: Pearl Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: This is the common oyster mushroom. Depending on substrate, light and temperature, pearl oysters will vary in coloration from white to grey and brown. More intense light will produce a darker coloration. Substrate: Pasteurized straw, Wood chips, Sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Pheasant Back (Polyporus squamosus)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: Wide Range

species.name: Phoenix Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius)
species.description: Phoenix Oyster (Pleurotus pulmonarius) is very similar to Pearl Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus) but resembles the lung/trumpet shape and usually brown in color. Also grows on conifers and prefers warmer climates compared to Pearl Oyster. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust, Pine sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-85F/50-82F

species.name: Pink Oyster (Pleurotus djamor)
species.description: Pink Oyster (Pleurotus djamor) is one of the most demanded by growers worldwide especially due to its impressive pink color and taste. It thrives in warmer temperatures, fruiting between 70-98F. These mushrooms need plenty of fresh air. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-85F/70-98F

species.name: Pink Oyster (Pleurotus salmoneostramineus)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-85F/70-98F

species.name: Polycephalomyces sp.
species.description: This polycephalomyces was found attached to the underside of a rotten log growing on a caterpillar.

species.name: Princess Pearl (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Pearl Oyster - Princess Pearl (Pleurotus ostreatus). Substrate: Pasteurized straw, Hardwood Sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-85F

species.name: Red Chanterelle (Cantharellus cinnabarinus)
species.description: Ranging from flamingo pink to a deep autumnal orange color. A rare, beautiful and delicious edible mushroom closely related to the Yellow Chanterelle with the same fruity aroma reminiscent of apricots. Chanterelles cannot be grown indoors — they are mycorrhizal and must form a relationship with conifer trees. It can sometimes take years or even decades for chanterelles to establish.

species.name: Red Reishi (Ganoderma resinaceum)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/65-75F

species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.name: Sajor Caju Oyster (Pleurotus sajor caju)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/70-85F

species.name: Sakura Oyster (Pleurotus djamor)
species.description: Pink Oyster - Sakura (Pleurotus djamor). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-85F/70-98F

species.name: Sanborn Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus) Wild Maine Strain
species.description: Maine wild clone found in a cemetery in bright constant sun — may be heat resistant. Grew all spring, summer and fall for 2 years in a row. Grows huge with brown caps. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-90F

species.name: Scarlet Caterpillarclub (Cordyceps militaris)
species.description: Cordyceps militaris is grown on a nutrient-enriched grain substrate. Colonize in the dark at 60-70F for 7-10 days, then expose to indirect sunlight or artificial light for 12 hours per day to initiate fruiting. Over 4-5 weeks the jars change color to orange and start producing mushroom fruit bodies. Never allow temps above 70F. Common substrates include brown rice with malt extract, yeast extract, and gypsum.

species.name: Shaggy Mane (Coprinus comatus)
species.description: Substrate: Straw, compost, sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/58-65F

species.name: Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) Cold Weather Strains
species.description: Cold weather Shiitake strains including: Shiitake (50-75F), Shiitake 034 (45-75F), Shiitake 3790 (55-65F), Shiitake Siberian Snap (48-75F), Shiitake Mocha (40-62F), Shiitake Callisto (40-64F), Shiitake Felicity (44-68F), Shiitake Blizzard (44-68F).

species.name: Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) Warm Weather Strains
species.description: Warm weather Shiitake strains including: Shiitake Alaskan Summer (48-78F), Shiitake Midnight Moon (55-80F), Shiitake Mordecai (50-80F).

species.name: Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) Wide Range Weather Strains
species.description: Wide range Shiitake strains including: Shiitake 3782 (50-75F), Shiitake Summer Solstice (54-75F), Shiitake Solar Eclipse (55-75F), Shiitake S75 (48-78F), Shiitake Summer Breeze (55-75F), Shiitake Southern Sky (55-75F).

species.name: Shiitake 5000 (Lentinula edodes)

species.name: Silky Sheath (Volvariella bombycina)
species.description: Fruit bodies grow singly or in small groups on trunks and decayed stumps of dead hardwoods. Favored species include sugar maple, red maple, silver maple, magnolia, mango, beech, oak, and elm. Often found in clefts and knotholes of dead or living tree trunks. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-78F/80-82F

species.name: Sky Blue Oyster (Pleurotus columbinus)
species.description: Blue Oyster - Sky Blue Oyster (Pleurotus columbinus). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/65-80F

species.name: Snow Fungus (Tremella fuciformis)
species.description: Snow Fungus (Tremella fuciformis) produces white, frond-like, gelatinous fruiting bodies. Widespread, especially in the tropics. One of the most popular fungi in the cuisine and medicine of China. Tremella fuciformis is a parasitic yeast, growing as a slimy film until it encounters its preferred host Annulohypoxylon archeri, then invades, triggering the aggressive mycelial growth required to form the fruiting bodies.

species.name: Snow White Oyster (Pleurotus ulmarius)
species.description: White Oyster - Snow White Oyster (Pleurotus ulmarius). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/50-65F

species.name: Sordid Blewit Bleu Foot (Clitocybe sordida)
species.description: Sordid Blewit is a somewhat smaller and less robust mushroom than the Wood Blewit, with deeper violet colors and a thinner cap margin when mature. Prefers high nitrogen and woody substrates but grows much faster than Wood Blewit. It seems to have a preference for layered hardwood and pine needle/pine chip duff mixed with layers of leaves and organic matter.

species.name: Split Gill (Schizophyllum commune)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: Wide Range

species.name: Straw Shiitake (Lentinula edodes)
species.description: Straw Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) is a good choice for any grower looking for a diverse Shiitake with a high biological efficiency. Grows on all the normal sawdust types as most shiitakes while also performing well on pasteurized straw and conifer type woods. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-78F/50-75F

species.name: Tarragon Oyster (Pleurotus eunosmus)
species.description: Tarragon Oyster Mushroom (Pleurotus eunosmus) is a very rare oyster mushroom thought to be found only in the British Isles and currently not commercially cultivated. With a distinctive trumpet shaped cap, its smell and taste resembles the herb tarragon, making it probably the finest tasting oyster mushroom. Isolated by Adrian Ogden from Gourmet Woodland Mushrooms from ancient woodlands in Yorkshire, England. Found growing on a large fallen beech tree. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Pine sawdust, Straw, cottonseed hulls, sugar cane, coffee, paper products. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/70-90F, Humidity: 90-95%

species.name: The Prince (Agaricus augustus)
species.description: Substrate: Manure and straw based composts. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 75-80F/65-77F

species.name: Tiered Tooth Fungus (Hericium cirrhatum)
species.description: Tiered Tooth Fungus (Hericium cirrhatum) is a very rare fungus that grows on dead wood of beech trees. When young and fresh they are generally considered choice edibles with a fine flavor and texture similar to fish or tender meat.

species.name: Tiger Sawgill (Lentinus tigrinus)
species.description: Cousin to the widely cultivated Shiitake, Tiger sawgill (Lentinus tigrinus) is native to the US and cultivated on hardwood logs outdoors and on hardwood sawdust indoors. Similar to the flavor of the Shiitake but the stems are tough. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-75F/75-90F

species.name: Tree Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus) Wild Strain
species.description: Cloned from a foot long oyster mushroom. This strain fruits massive clusters with big meaty and delicious caps. Fruits in hot or cold temperatures without any problems. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/60-70F

species.name: Turkey Tail (Trametes versicolor)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-80F/65-75F

species.description: Cloned from wild specimens found near a pond full of turtles, Greenbush Maine. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-75F/50-75F

species.name: Umbrella Polypore (Polyporus umbellatus)
species.description: Umbrella polypore is a rare, edible species of mushroom, found growing on roots of old beeches or oak.

species.name: Valentine Oyster (Pleurotus djamor)
species.description: Pink Oyster - Valentine (Pleurotus djamor). Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-85F/70-98F

species.name: Velvet Pioppino (Agrocybe aegerita)
species.description: Black Poplar - Velvet Pioppino (Agrocybe aegerita). Substrate: Hardwood sawdust / Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/50-60F

species.name: Warm Weather Button Tork (Agaricus bitorquis) Me A19
species.description: A warm temperature version of the common white button mushroom (Agaricus bisporus). 'Torks' are denser, stronger in flavor, higher in disease resistance and less sensitive to high CO2 levels than the button mushroom. More suitable for the home grower, especially in warm climates. Substrate: Manure and straw based composts. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 84-86F/75-77F

species.name: White Beech Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus)
species.description: Beech Clam / Buna Shimeji (Hypsizygus tessulatus) is an edible mushroom native to East Asia. Most often found on beech trees. Substrate: Hardwood sawdust, Straw. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/55-65F

species.name: White Button (Agaricus bisporus)
species.description: Substrate: Manure and straw based composts.

species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-78F/55-60F

species.name: White Elm Mushroom (Hypsizygus ulmarius) Real
species.description: Hypsizygus ulmarius grows solitary or in small clusters on wounds of living hardwoods, particularly elm and boxelder. Often found high up in the tree through the months of August to December. This is the TRUE White Elm Mushroom (Hypsizygus ulmarius) culture, not the more common easier to cultivate White Elm Oyster (Pleurotus ulmarius).

species.name: White Elm Oyster Hypsizygus (Pleurotus ulmarius)
species.description: Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-75F/50-65F

species.name: White Ferula (Pleurotus nebrodensis)
species.description: Substrate: Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 65-78F/55-60F

species.name: Whitelaced Shank (Megacollybia platyphylla)
species.description: Whitelaced Shank (Megacollybia platyphylla) is a saprobic mushroom (feeding on rotting wood and other organic vegetation) that can occur either solitarily or in small groups on and near deciduous hardwood trunks, branches or woody debris.

species.name: Wine Cap (Stropharia rugoso annulata)
species.description: Wine Cap (Stropharia rugoso-annulata) is a large and adaptive edible species best suited for outdoor cultivation. Indoor cultivation is possible but requires an unsterile casing and is slow to fruit. Best to bury a fully colonized block outside in the spring or use as spawn to create outdoor beds. Substrate: hardwood chips and sawdust, straw and composts. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/60-70F

species.name: Wine Cap (Stropharia rugoso annulata) Wild Strain
species.description: Wild Strain. Wine Cap (Stropharia rugoso-annulata) is a large and adaptive edible species best suited for outdoor cultivation. Substrate: hardwood chips and sawdust, straw and composts. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/60-70F

species.name: Wine Cap Golden (Stropharia rugosoannulata) Var Lutea
species.description: Wine Cap (Stropharia rugoso-annulata) golden variety. Best suited for outdoor cultivation. Substrate: hardwood chips and sawdust, straw and composts. Colonization/Fruiting Temperatures: 70-80F/60-70F

species.name: Winter Oyster (Pleurotus ostreatus)
species.description: Cloned from a wild Pleurotus ostreatus found growing during winter. This one loves the cooler temps. Substrate: Straw, Hardwood sawdust. Colonizing/Fruiting Temps: 70-75F/45-70F

species.name: Wood Blewit (Lepista nuda) Wild Strain
species.description: Wood Blewit is a fall fruiting mushroom that appears randomly where there is plenty of surface forest litter. It seems to have a preference for layered hardwood and pine needle/pine chip duff mixed with layers of leaves and organic matter. Blewits take more than a growing season to establish.
